topic: What Electrical Engineering Is and How Power Reaches Your Home
title: How Power Travels Explained Simply | Basic Electrical Engineering Ep 1
description:
Seven in the evening in Suryagaon, a village in north Karnataka, and the lights go out again. Kittu asks his sister Meera, a first-year electrical engineering student, one simple question: where does our electricity even come from? In this animated lesson we answer it, and learn what electrical engineering really is.

You will follow the power live, from a generator at a power station, through a step up transformer, across tall transmission towers, down through a substation and the pole transformer, past the meter to the switch. Then a side-by-side run shows why lines use very high voltage: send 100 kW down a 1 ohm line at 1,000 V and 10 kW is wasted as heat; at 10,000 V only 100 W is lost, because the loss grows with the current squared (example figures). We watch alternating current trace live at your socket: 230 V, 50 Hz, with each swing peaking near 325 V. We see the same chain at work today in a power station control room, India's national grid, a hospital and a metro railway, and we look at the human side honestly, with lineman Shankar anna's rule for live wires and a piece of Karnataka history from 1902.

This is Episode 1 of Basic Electrical Engineering, the common first-year course for every B.E. and B.Tech branch in India and Year 1 of our Engineering Electrical (EEE) series.
